subject: Deployment pricing deltas: hosted baseline vs Dedicated vs Private
messages:
From: Susan Jones <susan.jones@storix.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: hosted vs Dedicated vs Private pricing cross-walk

Hi Neha,

Thanks for taking this. We're evaluating Redwood for two streams: a customer-facing chat feature (high qps, many short responses) and a batch embedding pipeline for search (large monthly volume). Procurement asked for a simple cross-walk that shows:
- baseline Hosted API economics (per-token and embeddings)
- how unit cost changes with Dedicated (committed capacity)
- what changes for Private (license, infra, PS, and ongoing support)

Can you send a spreadsheet or one-pager that lays this out with example math for 5M monthly tokens and 200M embeddings units? Also flag any minimums, lead times, and standard SLA differences between modes.

We have a procurement checklist attached and would like to see an initial commercial view before scheduling a tapestry call with legal/finance.

Best,
Susan
Director of Product
Storix Inc.

Attachments: Storix_procurement_checklist.pdf

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Susan Jones <susan.jones@storix.com>
Cc: Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-09T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: hosted vs Dedicated vs Private pricing cross-walk

Hi Susan — thanks for the clear ask and attachment. I've attached an initial pricing_crosswalk_v1.xlsx that summarizes baseline hosted rates and example math for the volumes you called out. Highlights in plain text below so it's searchable.

Quick summary (examples only):
- Hosted API (baseline): $0.50 per 1k input tokens, $1.25 per 1k output tokens; embeddings $0.75 per 1k vectors (standard dims). No minimum commit; pay-as-you-go.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pool): unit cost reduction depends on commit tier — typically 25% reduction at $50k/month commit, 40% reduction at $150k+/month. There is also a base pool management fee (example: $10k/month for reserved pool administration and priority capacity). Support & SLA improve with Dedicated (SLA credits available above commit).
- Private (VPC or on-prem): licensing + deployment. Typical structure: one-time license/installation (example: $250k), annual platform fee (example: ~18% of license), professional services for onboarding ($40k–$120k depending on scope), plus infrastructure OPEX (customer-managed). Private offers the strongest data isolation and optional air-gapped installs.

A few notes and asks:
- Attached sheet has example cost buckets and a column for "expected P95 latency" by mode. If you can share the expected qps profile (p95 request size, concurrency, and embedding batch size), we can refine CPU/GPU sizing and a tighter quote.
- Are you targeting a 12-month or 36-month commit for Dedicated? Discounts and PS pricing change with term.
- We can prepare a draft term sheet once you confirm target commit and SLAs.

Propose a 30-min call on Tuesday to walk the spreadsheet with Connor (solutions + pricing). 

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

Attachments: pricing_crosswalk_v1.xlsx

From: Susan Jones <susan.jones@storix.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-10T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: hosted vs Dedicated vs Private pricing cross-walk

Neha — thanks for the fast turnaround and the workbook. Quick answers and follow-ups:

- We're likely to scope for a 12–24 month initial commitment window, with the ability to convert to a longer commit if performance and cost align.
- Attached is our rough usage estimate (Storix_usage_estimate.xlsx). For the chat workload, expect high QPS at launch (bursts to ~300 rps) with median response length ~80 tokens, p95 ~320 tokens. For embeddings, 200M vectors/month (batch jobs overnight).
- Procurement is particularly interested in: whether Dedicated discounts can stack with quantization/low-precision model variants (i.e., do we get the committed discount + lower model-cost from quantized variants?). Also want clarity on overage charges and how burst-to-hosted fallback would be billed if Dedicated is at capacity.
- One ask: can Redwood provide a one-off pilot credit (we're a startup with limited up-front spend) or trial credits applied to first invoice? That helps justify short-term pilots with our execs.

I'll join a quick call — Tuesday works. Also attaching our procurement checklist as requested.

Thanks,
Susan

Attachments: Storix_usage_estimate.xlsx

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-10T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Request: hosted vs Dedicated vs Private pricing cross-walk

Connor / Marissa — looping you both in on Storix (attached usage and procurement checklist). They want a cross-walk and clarity on the following negotiation points:

1) Dedicated pricing: customer asks if committed discount stacks with lower-cost model variants (quantized). My read: yes — committed unit discount applies to the platform unit price; quantized model runtime reduces per-token compute cost which we typically bake into the "effective unit" recommendations. Need Connor to confirm the math cadence and how we show this in the term sheet column.

2) Overage / burst: they explicitly called out burst-to-hosted fallback. What is recommended billing for that? We can either bill overage at hosted list rates or offer metered fallback credits if they maintain a minimum buffer. Need guidance.

3) Pilot credit: they asked for a one-off pilot credit to offset first month for proof-of-concept. Any internal guardrails for credits or promo approvals?

4) Private: they want a sample budget for license + PS + 1 year of support + approximate infra guidance. PS estimate in the workbook is rough; please sanity-check.

Proposed next step: Connor to update the workbook with sample committed tiers and a short term-sheet bullet list; Marissa to approve discounting strategy if we need to offer an introductory concession (they're an early-stage acct — small logo value but good product fit). Can we aim to have a draft term sheet by Monday EOD?

Thanks — Neha

From: Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-11T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Request: hosted vs Dedicated vs Private pricing cross-walk

Thanks for the context. Quick answers and proposed numbers to populate the workbook: 

- Quantized model stacking: confirm — committed discounts apply to list unit price. If customer chooses a quantized runtime variant that reduces our infra cost by X%, we typically reflect that as a model selection/efficiency line item in the contract but the commit discount is multiplicative on the quoted effective unit. I'll add an example row showing Hosted list -> quantized runtime -> Dedicated commit -> net unit price.

- Example baseline numbers to start with (we'll refine after sizing):
  * Hosted list (example): $0.50 / 1k input tokens, $1.25 / 1k output tokens, $0.75 / 1k embeddings units.
  * Dedicated commit tiers: 25% off at $50k/mo, 40% off at $150k+/mo. Dedicated also has a management fee we typically show as $10k/mo (can be credited back into commit for larger deals).
  * Private: one-time license $250k, PS $40k (small), PS up to $120k for complex infra; annual support 18% list. Infra costs are customer-run — we'll provide guidance but not include public cloud compute costs in our line items.

- Overage billing: recommend default approach = overage billed at hosted list rates monthly. For negotiation, we can offer a "burst buffer" add-on (metered credits) for first 3 months at a small incremental fee. I'll add a sample line: 10% burst buffer included in year 1 for $5k/mo.

- Pilot credits: standard guardrail = credits <= 10% of expected first-year ARR and require approval if > $25k. For a startup pilot, we can offer a one-time $7,500 credit applied to the first invoice. Marissa, approve?

I'll update pricing_crosswalk_v1.xlsx with the rows above and include example math for Storix's usage numbers. Also I'll draft a short term sheet (one page) that includes these options and the pilot credit. Expect updates by Monday EOD.

—Connor
Head of Solutions Pricing | Redwood Inference

From: Susan Jones <susan.jones@storix.com>

Subject: Re: Deployment pricing deltas: hosted baseline vs Dedicated vs Private

Thanks all — that's exactly the level of detail we needed. Appreciate the sample numbers and the pilot credit guidance. Next items on our side:
- I'll circulate the internal exec summary and confirm if Storix will target a 12-month or 24-month commit window by Friday.
- Please send the updated workbook and the draft term sheet when ready. If you can also include a short appendix that explains how burst-to-hosted fallback billing would appear on our invoices (example line items), that'll help procurement sign-off.

Let's pencil a follow-up call for next Wednesday to review the term sheet.

Best,
Susan
